"""Clean the plan-administration renewal exports.

Reads  renewals_2025_export.csv  (last year's renewals, with outcome)
       renewals_due_export.csv   (plans due in the next three months)
Writes renewals_2025.csv and renewals_due.csv:
  snake_case columns, one row per plan, consistent labels/units,
  and in the history `terminated` = Yes (employer left) / No.

Usage: python clean.py
"""
import re

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

MISSING = {"", "-", "n/a", "na", "unknown", "none", "null"}

PROV = {
    "on": "ON", "ont": "ON", "ont.": "ON", "ontario": "ON",
    "qc": "QC", "pq": "QC", "quebec": "QC", "québec": "QC",
    "bc": "BC", "b.c.": "BC", "british columbia": "BC",
    "ab": "AB", "alta": "AB", "alberta": "AB",
    "mb": "MB", "man.": "MB", "manitoba": "MB",
    "sk": "SK", "sask": "SK", "saskatchewan": "SK",
    "ns": "NS", "nova scotia": "NS",
    "nb": "NB", "new brunswick": "NB",
    "nl": "NL", "newfoundland": "NL",
    "pe": "PE", "pei": "PE", "p.e.i.": "PE",
}
INDUSTRY = {
    "professional services": "Professional Services", "professional svcs": "Professional Services",
    "prof. services": "Professional Services",
    "manufacturing": "Manufacturing", "mfg.": "Manufacturing", "mfg": "Manufacturing",
    "non-profit": "Non-Profit", "nfp": "Non-Profit", "public sector/nfp": "Non-Profit",
    "retail": "Retail", "retail trade": "Retail",
    "construction": "Construction", "constr": "Construction",
    "technology": "Technology", "tech": "Technology", "it/software": "Technology",
    "health care": "Health Care", "healthcare": "Health Care",
}
PLAN_TYPE = {
    "health & dental": "Health & Dental", "h&d": "Health & Dental",
    "health and dental": "Health & Dental", "health/dental": "Health & Dental",
    "health, dental & life": "Health, Dental & Life", "hdl": "Health, Dental & Life",
    "h/d/life": "Health, Dental & Life",
    "full package": "Full Package (incl. LTD)", "full benefits (incl. ltd)": "Full Package (incl. LTD)",
    "full": "Full Package (incl. LTD)", "h/d/l/ltd": "Full Package (incl. LTD)",
}
FUNDING = {
    "fully insured": "Fully Insured", "insured": "Fully Insured",
    "pooled": "Pooled",
    "aso": "ASO", "a.s.o.": "ASO", "admin services only": "ASO",
}
CHANNEL = {
    "broker": "Broker", "brkr": "Broker",
    "consultant": "Consultant", "benefits consultant": "Consultant", "cons.": "Consultant",
    "direct": "Direct", "in-house": "Direct",
}
BILLING = {
    "pad": "Pre-authorized debit", "auto debit": "Pre-authorized debit",
    "pre-authorized debit": "Pre-authorized debit",
    "eft": "EFT", "wire/eft": "EFT",
    "cheque": "Cheque/Invoice", "check": "Cheque/Invoice", "cheque/invoice": "Cheque/Invoice",
    "invoice": "Cheque/Invoice",
}
YESNO = {"y": "Yes", "yes": "Yes", "true": "Yes", "1": "Yes",
         "n": "No", "no": "No", "false": "No", "0": "No"}
# "In force" rows are spread evenly over every renewal month of 2025, so they
# are plans still active after renewal, i.e. renewed.
STATUS = {"renewed": "No", "in force": "No",
          "terminated": "Yes", "term": "Yes", "moved carrier": "Yes"}

RENAME = {
    "Plan ID": "plan_id", "Renewal Date": "renewal_date",
    "Plan Effective Date": "plan_effective_date", "Prov": "province",
    "Industry": "industry", "Lives Covered": "lives_covered", "Plan Type": "plan_type",
    "Funding": "funding", "Annual Premium": "annual_premium",
    "Renewal Increase": "renewal_increase_pct", "Loss Ratio (12m)": "loss_ratio_pct_12m",
    "Channel": "channel", "Billing": "billing", "Late Pmts (12m)": "late_payments_12m",
    "Account Reviews (12m)": "account_reviews_12m", "Service Issues (12m)": "service_issues_12m",
    "Online Admin?": "online_admin", "Wellness Program?": "wellness_program",
    "Member App Use %": "member_app_use_pct", "Renewal Status": "terminated",
}


def is_missing(s):
    return s is None or (isinstance(s, float) and np.isnan(s)) or str(s).strip().lower() in MISSING


def mapper(table, col):
    def f(s):
        if is_missing(s):
            return np.nan
        key = str(s).strip().lower()
        if key not in table:
            raise ValueError(f"{col}: unmapped label {s!r}")
        return table[key]
    return f


def to_number(s):
    if is_missing(s):
        return np.nan
    t = re.sub(r"(?i)cad|\$|,|%|\s", "", str(s))
    return float(t)


def loss_ratio(s):
    """Loss ratio arrives as '85.0%' or as a fraction '0.85'; return percent."""
    if is_missing(s):
        return np.nan
    v = to_number(s)
    return v if "%" in str(s) else v * 100


def lives(s):
    v = to_number(s)
    # -1 and 999999-style values are placeholder codes, not head counts.
    if np.isnan(v) or v <= 0 or v > 5000:
        return np.nan
    return v


def dates(col):
    return pd.to_datetime(col.str.strip(), format="mixed").dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")


def clean(path):
    raw = pd.read_csv(path, dtype=str, keep_default_na=False)
    n0 = len(raw)
    raw = raw[raw["Plan ID"].str.match(r"^GB-\d+$")]          # drops the TOTAL footer
    n_footer = n0 - len(raw)
    raw = raw.drop_duplicates()
    n_dup = n0 - n_footer - len(raw)
    if raw["Plan ID"].duplicated().any():
        raise ValueError(f"{path}: conflicting rows for the same Plan ID")

    d = raw.rename(columns=RENAME)
    out = pd.DataFrame({"plan_id": d["plan_id"].str.strip()})
    out["renewal_date"] = dates(d["renewal_date"])
    out["plan_effective_date"] = dates(d["plan_effective_date"])
    out["tenure_years"] = ((pd.to_datetime(out["renewal_date"]) - pd.to_datetime(out["plan_effective_date"]))
                           .dt.days / 365.25).round(1)
    out["province"] = d["province"].map(mapper(PROV, "province"))
    out["industry"] = d["industry"].map(mapper(INDUSTRY, "industry"))
    out["lives_covered"] = d["lives_covered"].map(lives).astype("Int64")
    out["plan_type"] = d["plan_type"].map(mapper(PLAN_TYPE, "plan_type"))
    out["funding"] = d["funding"].map(mapper(FUNDING, "funding"))
    out["annual_premium"] = d["annual_premium"].map(to_number).round(2)
    out["renewal_increase_pct"] = d["renewal_increase_pct"].map(to_number)
    out["loss_ratio_pct_12m"] = d["loss_ratio_pct_12m"].map(loss_ratio).round(1)
    out["channel"] = d["channel"].map(mapper(CHANNEL, "channel"))
    out["billing"] = d["billing"].map(mapper(BILLING, "billing"))
    for c in ["late_payments_12m", "account_reviews_12m", "service_issues_12m"]:
        out[c] = d[c].map(to_number).astype("Int64")
    out["online_admin"] = d["online_admin"].map(mapper(YESNO, "online_admin"))
    out["wellness_program"] = d["wellness_program"].map(mapper(YESNO, "wellness_program"))
    out["member_app_use_pct"] = d["member_app_use_pct"].map(to_number)
    if "terminated" in d:
        out["terminated"] = d["terminated"].map(mapper(STATUS, "terminated"))

    print(f"{path}: {n0} rows -> {len(out)} plans "
          f"(dropped {n_footer} footer/total row(s), {n_dup} exact duplicate rows)")
    miss = out.isna().sum()
    print("  missing after cleaning:", miss[miss > 0].to_dict())
    return out


if __name__ == "__main__":
    clean("renewals_2025_export.csv").to_csv("renewals_2025.csv", index=False)
    clean("renewals_due_export.csv").to_csv("renewals_due.csv", index=False)

Reads  renewals_2025_export.csv  (last year's renewals, with outcome)
       renewals_due_export.csv   (plans due in the next three months)
Writes renewals_2025.csv and renewals_due.csv:
  snake_case columns, one row per plan, consistent labels/units,
  and in the history `terminated` = Yes (employer left) / No.

Usage: python clean.py

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

MISSING = {"", "-", "n/a", "na", "unknown", "none", "null"}

    "on": "ON", "ont": "ON", "ont.": "ON", "ontario": "ON",
    "qc": "QC", "pq": "QC", "quebec": "QC", "québec": "QC",
    "bc": "BC", "b.c.": "BC", "british columbia": "BC",
    "ab": "AB", "alta": "AB", "alberta": "AB",

    "ns": "NS", "n.s.": "NS", "nova scotia": "NS",
    "nb": "NB", "n.b.": "NB", "new brunswick": "NB",
    "nl": "NL", "nfld": "NL", "newfoundland": "NL",
    "pe": "PE", "pei": "PE", "p.e.i.": "PE",
}
INDUSTRY = {
    "professional services": "Professional Services", "professional svcs": "Professional Services",
    "prof. services": "Professional Services",
    "manufacturing": "Manufacturing", "mfg.": "Manufacturing", "mfg": "Manufacturing",
    "non-profit": "Non-Profit", "nfp": "Non-Profit", "public sector/nfp": "Non-Profit",
    "retail": "Retail", "retail trade": "Retail",
    "construction": "Construction", "constr": "Construction",
    "technology": "Technology", "tech": "Technology", "it/software": "Technology",
    "health care": "Health Care", "healthcare": "Health Care",
}
PLAN_TYPE = {
    "health & dental": "Health & Dental", "h&d": "Health & Dental",
    "health and dental": "Health & Dental", "health/dental": "Health & Dental",
    "health, dental & life": "Health, Dental & Life", "hdl": "Health, Dental & Life",
    "h/d/life": "Health, Dental & Life",
    "full package": "Full Package (incl. LTD)", "full benefits (incl. ltd)": "Full Package (incl. LTD)",
    "full": "Full Package (incl. LTD)", "h/d/l/ltd": "Full Package (incl. LTD)",
}
FUNDING = {
    "fully insured": "Fully Insured", "insured": "Fully Insured",
    "pooled": "Pooled",
    "aso": "ASO", "a.s.o.": "ASO", "admin services only": "ASO",
}
CHANNEL = {
    "broker": "Broker", "brkr": "Broker",
    "consultant": "Consultant", "benefits consultant": "Consultant", "cons.": "Consultant",
    "direct": "Direct", "in-house": "Direct",
}
BILLING = {
    "pad": "Pre-authorized debit", "auto debit": "Pre-authorized debit",
    "pre-authorized debit": "Pre-authorized debit",
    "eft": "EFT", "wire/eft": "EFT",
    "cheque": "Cheque/Invoice", "check": "Cheque/Invoice", "cheque/invoice": "Cheque/Invoice",
    "invoice": "Cheque/Invoice",
}
YESNO = {"y": "Yes", "yes": "Yes", "true": "Yes", "1": "Yes",
         "n": "No", "no": "No", "false": "No", "0": "No"}
# "In force" rows are spread evenly over every renewal month of 2025, so they
# are plans still active after renewal, i.e. renewed.
STATUS = {"renewed": "No", "in force": "No",
          "terminated": "Yes", "term": "Yes", "moved carrier": "Yes"}

RENAME = {
    "Plan ID": "plan_id", "Renewal Date": "renewal_date",
    "Plan Effective Date": "plan_effective_date", "Prov": "province",
    "Industry": "industry", "Lives Covered": "lives_covered", "Plan Type": "plan_type",
    "Funding": "funding", "Annual Premium": "annual_premium",
    "Renewal Increase": "renewal_increase_pct", "Loss Ratio (12m)": "loss_ratio_pct_12m",
    "Channel": "channel", "Billing": "billing", "Late Pmts (12m)": "late_payments_12m",
    "Account Reviews (12m)": "account_reviews_12m", "Service Issues (12m)": "service_issues_12m",
    "Online Admin?": "online_admin", "Wellness Program?": "wellness_program",
    "Member App Use %": "member_app_use_pct", "Renewal Status": "terminated",
}


def is_missing(s):
    return s is None or (isinstance(s, float) and np.isnan(s)) or str(s).strip().lower() in MISSING


def mapper(table, col):
    def f(s):
        if is_missing(s):
            return np.nan
        key = str(s).strip().lower()
        if key not in table:
            raise ValueError(f"{col}: unmapped label {s!r}")
        return table[key]
    return f


def to_number(s):
    if is_missing(s):
        return np.nan
    t = re.sub(r"(?i)cad|\$|,|%|\s", "", str(s))
    return float(t)


def loss_ratio(s):
    """Loss ratio arrives as '85.0%' or as a fraction '0.85'; return percent."""
    if is_missing(s):
        return np.nan
    v = to_number(s)
    return v if "%" in str(s) else v * 100


def lives(s):
    v = to_number(s)
    # -1 and 999999-style values are placeholder codes, not head counts.
    if np.isnan(v) or v <= 0 or v > 5000:
        return np.nan
    return v


def dates(col):
    return pd.to_datetime(col.str.strip(), format="mixed").dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")


def clean(path):
    raw = pd.read_csv(path, dtype=str, keep_default_na=False)
    n0 = len(raw)
    raw = raw[raw["Plan ID"].str.match(r"^GB-\d+$")]          # drops the TOTAL footer
    n_footer = n0 - len(raw)
    raw = raw.drop_duplicates()
    n_dup = n0 - n_footer - len(raw)
    if raw["Plan ID"].duplicated().any():
        raise ValueError(f"{path}: conflicting rows for the same Plan ID")

    d = raw.rename(columns=RENAME)
    out = pd.DataFrame({"plan_id": d["plan_id"].str.strip()})
    out["renewal_date"] = dates(d["renewal_date"])
    out["plan_effective_date"] = dates(d["plan_effective_date"])
    out["tenure_years"] = ((pd.to_datetime(out["renewal_date"]) - pd.to_datetime(out["plan_effective_date"]))
                           .dt.days / 365.25).round(1)
    out["province"] = d["province"].map(mapper(PROV, "province"))
    out["industry"] = d["industry"].map(mapper(INDUSTRY, "industry"))
    out["lives_covered"] = d["lives_covered"].map(lives).astype("Int64")
    out["plan_type"] = d["plan_type"].map(mapper(PLAN_TYPE, "plan_type"))
    out["funding"] = d["funding"].map(mapper(FUNDING, "funding"))
    out["annual_premium"] = d["annual_premium"].map(to_number).round(2)
    out["renewal_increase_pct"] = d["renewal_increase_pct"].map(to_number)
    out["loss_ratio_pct_12m"] = d["loss_ratio_pct_12m"].map(loss_ratio).round(1)
    out["channel"] = d["channel"].map(mapper(CHANNEL, "channel"))
    out["billing"] = d["billing"].map(mapper(BILLING, "billing"))
    for c in ["late_payments_12m", "account_reviews_12m", "service_issues_12m"]:
        out[c] = d[c].map(to_number).astype("Int64")
    out["online_admin"] = d["online_admin"].map(mapper(YESNO, "online_admin"))
    out["wellness_program"] = d["wellness_program"].map(mapper(YESNO, "wellness_program"))
    out["member_app_use_pct"] = d["member_app_use_pct"].map(to_number)
    if "terminated" in d:
        out["terminated"] = d["terminated"].map(mapper(STATUS, "terminated"))

    print(f"{path}: {n0} rows -> {len(out)} plans "
          f"(dropped {n_footer} footer/total row(s), {n_dup} exact duplicate rows)")
    miss = out.isna().sum()
    print("  missing after cleaning:", miss[miss > 0].to_dict())
    return out


if __name__ == "__main__":
    clean("renewals_2025_export.csv").to_csv("renewals_2025.csv", index=False)
    clean("renewals_due_export.csv").to_csv("renewals_due.csv", index=False)

# Which employers are likely to leave at renewal, why, and what might keep them *For: Head of Group Retention. Prepared 22 November 2026 from the plan-administration exports.* ## The short version - **About 130–150 of the 1,200 plans renewing between mid-November and mid-February are likely to leave.** The two models we used give those two figures. The higher one is probably closer, because the main model ran about 3 points low when we tested it on last year's data. That is roughly $18M of annual premium at risk, out of $258M due. - **The risk is concentrated.** 85 plans have a 30% or higher chance of leaving. On last year's data, calling the top 20% of the list would have reached about **46% of the employers who left**, and about one in three of the plans called would actually have left. - **The strongest warning signs**, in order of how much the model relies on them: 1. no account review in the past year 2. small plans, measured by premium or lives covered 3. a large renewal increase, which goes with a high loss ratio 4. service issues 5. late payments 6. paying by cheque or invoice - **What looks most promising to act on: make sure every plan gets at least one account review before renewal.** In last year's data, plans with no review left at 19%, against 8% for plans with one. The gap holds for small and large plans and for good and bad loss ratios. **A second or third review showed no further benefit.** 71 of the 85 highest-risk plans due now have had no review. - **Capping renewal increases is not a good deal on these numbers.** The plans with big increases mostly have loss ratios over 100%. A 10% cap would give up about $1.6M of increase revenue to keep, on average, about $1.5M of premium on plans that are already losing money. - **These are patterns the model learned from last year, not proven effects.** The data cannot tell us whether reviews keep employers, or whether account managers simply review the accounts that are going to stay. The way to find out is a simple randomized test (see "What I recommend"). --- ## 1. Cleaning the exports (`clean.py`) `python clean.py` reads the two raw exports and writes `renewals_2025.csv` (6,000 plans) and `renewals_due.csv` (1,200 plans). | Problem in the export | What I did | |---|---| | 120 exact duplicate rows in the history and 12 in the due file | Removed. No plan had two *different* rows. | | 6 `TEST-000x` accounts and a `TOTAL` footer row in the history | Removed. They aren't real plans. | | Dates in four formats (`2025-03-03`, `2025/03/03`, `Mar 03, 2025`, `03-Mar-2025`) | Converted to `YYYY-MM-DD`. Added `tenure_years`, the years from the plan's start to its renewal. | | Loss ratio sometimes given as a percent (`85.0%`) and sometimes as a fraction (`0.85`) | Converted all to percent. | | Premiums written as `$74,848.88`, `CAD 9,676` or `62770.46` | Converted all to plain numbers. | | 34 spellings of the province, 21 of industry, 11 of plan type, 6 of funding, 9 of channel, 10 of billing, 10 of yes/no | Mapped to one label each. If a new spelling appears, the script stops with an error instead of guessing. | | Lives covered of `-1` or `999999`, plus `n/a`, `unknown` and `-` in several columns | Treated as missing: 113 values of lives covered, 242 of account reviews and 279 of app use in the history. | | Outcome labels `Renewed`, `RENEWED`, `In force`, `Terminated`, `TERM`, `moved carrier` | `terminated` = **Yes** for Terminated, TERM and moved carrier (764 plans, 12.7%). **No** for the rest. | **A judgment call you should know about.** I counted the 896 "In force" plans as renewed. They are spread evenly across every renewal month of 2025, so they are not a backlog of undecided renewals. They look like plans that are simply still active. If "In force" means something else in the admin system, the leave rate and the model would change. ## 2. How well last year predicts who leaves I held out a quarter of last year's plans and tested the models on them: | Model | ROC AUC (0.5 = coin flip, 1 = perfect) | |---|---| | TabICL (the model used for the scores) | 0.77 | | TabPFN (second opinion) | 0.76 | | Standard gradient boosting, for comparison | 0.74 | The scores are **good for ranking, not for certainty.** Even among the plans the model is most worried about, about half renew anyway. The model also misses some leavers entirely: about 40% of leavers fall outside the top 30% of the list. Results on the held-out plans: | If you contact the top… | …you reach this share of leavers | Share of contacted plans that actually left | |---|---|---| | 5% of plans | 18% | 51% | | 10% | 30% | 42% | | 20% | 46% | 32% | | 30% | 58% | 27% | The two models rank the due plans almost identically: rank correlation 0.985, and 89 of the same plans in each model's top 100. ## 3. I've cleaned both exports, scored all 1,200 plans due for renewal, and written up the findings in `report.md` for the head of group retention.

**How many will leave:** about 130–150 of the 1,200 due plans (mid-November to mid-February), or roughly $18M of the $258M premium due. The two models gave those two figures. The higher one is probably closer, because the main model ran about 3 points low when tested on last year's plans. 85 plans have a 30% or higher chance of leaving. On last year's data, contacting the top 20% of the list would have reached about 46% of the employers who actually left.

**Prediction quality:** it's good for ranking, not for certainty. On a held-out quarter of last year's plans the score was 0.77 (0.5 is a coin flip, 1 is perfect), against 0.74 for a standard model. Even among the highest-risk plans, about half renew anyway.

**Why they leave:** the strongest warning signs are:
- no account review in the past year
- a small plan
- a large renewal increase, which comes with a high loss ratio
- service issues
- late payments
- paying by cheque

These are patterns the model learned, not proven causes.

**What could keep them:**
- **One account review is the threshold.** Plans with no review left at 19%, against 8% with one review. The gap holds across plan sizes and loss ratios. A second review made no difference: −0.1 points (95% range −2.0 to +1.8), and the data could have detected a gap of 3.3 points. 71 of the 85 highest-risk plans have had no review. The causation could run the other way (account managers may skip accounts that are already leaving), so the report proposes a randomized test.
- **Capping increases doesn't pay.** Increase and loss ratio move together, and last year no plan with a loss ratio over 110% got an increase of 10% or less. So the cap scenarios go beyond what the data has seen. A 10% cap would also give up about $1.6M of increase revenue to keep about $1.5M of premium on plans losing money on claims (average loss ratio 113%).
- **Things that made little or no difference:** sales channel and EFT versus pre-authorized debit. The report gives the uncertainty and the smallest effect the data could have detected for each.

**Two things to check:**
- **"In force" status:** I counted these 896 plans as renewed, because they're spread evenly across every renewal month. If the admin system means something else by it, the results would change.
- **Dates already passed:** the due export includes 79 plans with renewal dates of 15–21 November. Six of them are high-risk, and their outcome may already be known.

**Changes to the approved plan:** I removed 6 test accounts and a TOTAL row, and used years since plan start instead of the raw dates for modelling. I also ran every what-if on a second model (both agreed closely) and added the cost-versus-premium-kept comparison for the price caps.

Files are in the working directory:
- `report.md`
- `clean.py`
- `renewals_2025.csv`
- `renewals_due.csv`
- `renewals_due_predictions.csv`
- `scenarios/` (what-if inputs and scores, held-out test files)
